newsitem.title: ALBANIA: New Albanian PM favours talks with rebels.
newsitem.headline: New Albanian PM favours talks with rebels.

text.p: New Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino said on Wednesday he favoured holding talks with armed rebels holding most of the south of the country and moving closer to the capital.

"I think this is not a time to issue orders on either side. It is a time for talks and dialogue," Fino told state television. "Not only my personal (links) but those of my government should be based on good understanding and cooperation with them so that they listen to our options and we listen to theirs."

A spokesman for armed rebels in the southern town of Sarande said on Wednesday the insurgents wanted a place at talks in Tirana between opposition parties and President Sali Berisha on forming an all-party government. Greece and Italy also called on authorities to start talks with the rebels.
Fino said his government's immediate priorities were tackling the large number of arms in private hands and righting the country's ruined economy.
"The people are armed. The economy is in ruins in many districts of Albania," he said. "And the third duty of this government is to prepare elections, free and democratic elections."
Fino, appointed by Berisha on Tuesday, is a member of the opposition socialists and a former mayor of Gjirokaster, one of the key southern towns held by the rebels.
